What is a Name Picker?

A Name Picker is a versatile tool for randomly selecting names from a list. It can pick a single winner or randomly assign people to teams. Perfect for classrooms, offices, game nights, or anywhere you need a fair selection without bias. Add names manually or paste a whole list at once.

When to Use the Name Picker

  • • Selecting winners for giveaways or raffles
  • • Randomly assigning people to teams
  • • Choosing who goes first in games
  • • Classroom activities or group projects
  • • Office decisions where everyone deserves equal chance

Pros

  • ✓ Pick single names or assign to teams
  • ✓ Add names one-by-one or bulk paste
  • ✓ Automatically removes picked names (optional)
  • ✓ Copy results or share with friends
  • ✓ Fair and unbiased selection every time

Considerations

  • • Need to add names before picking
  • • Team assignment is random, not balanced
  • • Duplicate names are automatically ignored
  • • Best for smaller groups (under 50 names)

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I add multiple names at once?

Use the "paste multiple names" text area. Enter names separated by commas or new lines, then click outside the box to add them all at once.

Can I use this for team assignments?

Yes! Switch to "Teams" mode, select how many teams you want (2-8), and click "Assign Teams". Names will be randomly shuffled and distributed across all teams.

How does the picked names feature work?

In "Pick One" mode, names that have been selected are grayed out and crossed off. This helps you keep track of who has already been picked, especially useful for multiple rounds.

Use the Name Picker to Teach Fairness and Equity

The Name Picker demonstrates what true fairness looks like: each name has an equal chance of being selected, with no manipulation or bias. When kids use this tool for choosing teams or picking partners, they're experiencing randomization as a fairness mechanism. This builds understanding that some decisions should be left to chance not because it's arbitrary, but because it's the most equitable approach.
